_schema.id: stable identifier, referenced in every report
_schema.question: the question as a user would ask it
_schema.answerable: true if the corpus contains the answer; false means the system SHOULD refuse
_schema.correct_books: file names in data/books/ that count as a correct retrieval (empty when unanswerable)
_schema.must_mention: required facts. Each fact is a list of accepted spellings -- the fact counts as present if ANY of them appears (case-insensitive). Old books spell things several ways (ourang-outang / orang-utan) and use curly apostrophes, so one spelling per fact would score the punctuation, not the answer.
_schema.nice_to_mention: optional facts; tracked but not required. TREC calls these 'okay' nuggets, as opposed to 'vital' ones.
_schema.note: why this question is in the set, and what failure it is meant to catch
_schema.must_not_appear: unanswerable questions only: giveaway words that must not occur in ANY book, or the trap has stopped being a trap. Checked by src/eval/verify_questions.py -- re-run it whenever books are added.
_schema.verification: every must_mention fact was checked by script to appear in the text of a correct book, and every trap was checked not to leak its giveaway words into any book
